ceramic.snippet:
Sabra Health Care REIT, Inc. (NYSE: SBRA) is a publicly traded real estate investment trust that specializes in healthcare-related properties. Its portfolio focuses on assets such as skilled nursing facilities, senior housing, hospitals, medical office buildings and other care-delivery sites. Sabra’s business model centers on acquiring, leasing and financing healthcare real estate to generate rental and mortgage income and to pay dividends to shareholders. The company’s performance is influenced by factors typical of healthcare REITs — tenant operating performance, government and private payer reimbursement rates, regulatory and licensing environments, interest rates and demographic trends such as an aging population. Sabra is managed to balance income generation and portfolio risk through asset selection, lease structuring and active portfolio management. Investors should consider both the potential income characteristics of healthcare real estate and the sector-specific operational and regulatory risks when evaluating SBRA.

Sabra Health Care REIT, Inc. reported second-quarter 2026 results with revenue of $235.9M, up from $189.2M a year earlier, while net income attributable to Sabra was a loss of $(25.2)M and diluted EPS was $(0.10) for the quarter.
Financial Highlights
- Revenue was $235.9M for Q2 2026, compared with $189.2M in Q2 2025; YoY change 24.7%.
- Net income was $(25.2)M attributable to Sabra for Q2 2026, versus $65.5M in Q2 2025.
- Diluted EPS was $(0.10) for Q2 2026, versus $0.27 in Q2 2025.
Business Highlights
- Portfolio growth: Completed acquisitions of seven senior housing managed communities and three skilled nursing facilities, expanding the company's managed portfolio.
- Revenue mix shift: Managed operations increased the share of resident-fee revenue versus traditional rental income, driving the year-over-year revenue increase.
- Operational performance: Managed communities saw higher occupancy and rates, though operating expenses rose due to labor costs, staffing and outsourced dining.
- Asset optimization: Executed disposals and selective acquisitions, generating net gains on sales and reallocating capital toward higher-quality assets.

Reimbursement trends among nursing homes remain positive while investment opportunities are rising, said leaders at Sabra Health Care REIT Inc. (Nasdaq: SBRA), who also noted that the company’s occupancy recovery looks promising.

During the second quarter, Sabra reported net income of 10 cents per diluted common share, a slight decrease compared to 9 cents in Q2 2023. Funds from operations (FFO) was 35 cents per diluted common share for Q2, beating Wall Street estimates by a penny, but lower compared to 33 cents in Q2 2023.

Sabra increased its annual earnings guidance to 48 cents to 51 cents for net income, and $1.33 to $1.36 for FFO, and both are attributable to common stockholders, per diluted common share.

The update follows portfolio momentum as the year has progressed, Sabra CEO Rick Matros said during the company’s Q2 earnings call on Thursday.

“Skilled nursing margins and rent coverage are higher than pre-pandemic levels, with the potential for further gains as occupancy continues to recover,” said Matros, adding that Sabra has approximately $906 million in liquidity.

Skilled nursing and seniors housing occupancy increased, Matros said, but on the SNF side is still about 200 basis points lower than pre-pandemic occupancy.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, rent, and management fees (EBITARM) margins, on the other hand, are now higher than pre-pandemic margins.

“The opportunity to reap the benefit of operating leverage is even greater, given the potential of occupancy growth,” Sabra Chief Investment Officer Talia Nevo-Hacohen said of the REIT’s domestic assets.

As for contract labor among Sabra assets, it has been at its lowest since March 2021, and agency use is down 50% compared to this time last year, executives said.

Meanwhile, Medicaid rate increases were positive and estimated to be roughly 7% across Sabra’s operating states – that’s 200 basis points higher than last year’s increases, Matros said.
